sentence_stem: If I had known about the delay,
correct_completion: I would have taken an earlier train.
full_sentence: If I had known about the delay, I would have taken an earlier train.
acceptable_variants: I would have chosen a different departure time.
I would have caught the earlier train.

options.text: I would take the same train again.
options.why_wrong: The present conditional does not match the unreal past meaning set up by 'had known', which needs a past conditional result.

options.text: I would have taken an earlier train.
I will take an earlier train tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: A future statement breaks the third conditional pattern started by 'if I had known', which refers to the past.

options.text: I took the earlier train, as I did last week.
options.why_wrong: The simple past reports a completed habit, not the imagined alternative that an unreal past condition requires.

grammar_focus: Third conditional: unreal past with 'if' and 'would have'
explanation: After 'if' with a past perfect clause, the main clause uses 'would have' plus a past participle to describe an imagined past result. Polish speakers may use a simple conditional without 'have' here, because Polish marks the unreal past with a single auxiliary-like form and does not separate present and past conditional forms in the same way.
translation: Gdybym wiedział o opóźnieniu, wziąłbym wcześniejszy pociąg.
